chronology: Recap: Othon von Salza, after killing his son and being castrated, creates the first Metabaronic weapons and converts the Castaka fortress on Okhar into a maxi-protonic tower.
Othon answers the Emperor's call, defeats pirates at the Golden Planet holding the Imperial offspring, and is knighted Metabaron.
The Empress sends Honorata, a Shabda-Oud priestess and last of the Von Salzas, to Okhar; Othon's jealous servants interrupt their first encounter.
During a lunar eclipse with a mass protoglow-worm mating event, Othon confesses to Honorata that a union is impossible due to his castration.
Honorata explains she cannot pass on the White Castaka birthmark and proposes blood-ritual conception; they link nervous systems and Honorata conceives from a drop of Othon's blood.
In the ninth month of pregnancy, Othon's two daughters seize Honorata and throw themselves with her from the top of his tower.
A dart carrying an epiphyte strikes Honorata during the fall; wind carries her suspended body while Othon pursues in a metacraft.
Honorata gives birth suspended between sky and ground; the infant is weightless because the epiphyte penetrated the embryonic sac and installed itself in his cells.
Honorata reveals she was sent by the Oiders to produce a perfect androgyne for a succession plot against Janus-Jana, but defied orders out of love and bore a son.
Honorata and Othon agree to conceal the child's sex for seven years before an unavoidable handover; Othon vows to use the interval to train the boy as a warrior.
Iko-Itta commits suicide, removing a threat to the child; Othon publicly bans the tribe from his fortress and replaces household staff with robots.
The infant is formally named Aghnar.
Aghnar is discovered to levitate; cause identified as the epiphyte in his cells.
Othon moves to kill Aghnar as unfit; Honorata reveals permanent sterility from the blood conception, making Aghnar their only possible child; an unnamed figure volunteers to train him in Shabda-Oud.
Othon imposes a seven-year blackout on news of the child and sets warrior trial terms: failure means death for both Aghnar and Othon.
Honorata takes Aghnar into exile at Anasirma, a sacred mountain forbidden for centuries; they are attacked by carnivorous eodactyls and shelter in a crystal cave.
Honorata and Aghnar survive in the crystal cave on woolly toads; at age five Aghnar is ordered to kill his toad companion as a lesson that duty supersedes love.
Honorata trains Aghnar with escalating weights, daily combat, Shabda-Oud meditation, and pain suppression via auto-hypnosis; he internalizes total distrust including of his mother.
Aghnar defeats Honorata in combat and resists her hypnotic waves; she gives him the only kiss of his childhood.
On the eve of his seventh birthday, Honorata and Aghnar ride a trained eodactyl at dawn to the Castaka fortress.
Othon and Honorata reunite after seven years; Aghnar's initiation begins immediately.
Aghnar faces a robo-killer whose sole weak point is a red button on its chest and which grows a new arm every ten minutes; after over an hour Aghnar triggers its self-destruct.
Judges dispute the legitimacy of the win given Aghnar's weightlessness but honor their prior oath, accept him as a future Metabaron, and add a pain-endurance trial.
Aghnar endures a voice-keyed foot-crushing capsule administered by Othon without yielding; the device destroys his feet.
Aghnar's feet are replaced with metal prosthetics, increasing his weight and granting superhuman power; bodily mutilation is established as a component of Metabaronic initiation.
locations: Okhar — home planet of the Castaka fortress and Othon's maxi-protonic tower
Castaka fortress — Othon's stronghold, site of Honorata's arrival and Aghnar's initiation trials
Golden Planet — Imperial court location where Othon was knighted Metabaron
Anasirma — sacred mountain forbidden for centuries, with deadly chasms and carnivorous eodactyls
Crystal cave on Anasirma — site of Honorata and Aghnar's seven-year exile, filled with soft whispering crystals and woolly toads
lore_laws: The title of Metabaron is formally bestowed by the Emperor as a knighthood earned through extraordinary service.
The White Castaka birthmark is hereditary and determines whether an heir can legitimately continue the line.
Conception via a nervous-system-linked blood ritual is possible but permanently destroys the mother's fertility.
An epiphyte delivered by dart can suspend a body in air; if it penetrates an embryonic sac it installs in fetal cells and causes permanent weightlessness.
A metacraft is a vehicle capable of aerial pursuit and recovery over long distances.
The Shabda-Oud discipline encompasses secret combat techniques, meditation, auto-hypnosis for pain suppression, and hypnotic-wave projection.
Metabaronic initiation requires the candidate to endure and survive bodily mutilation; augmented prosthetics are the expected replacement.
The Oiders hold authority to mandate assassination of parents, child, and associates if a forbidden birth is exposed.
Eodactyls are large carnivorous flying predators that can be trained as rideable mounts.
A voice-keyed crushing mechanism that stops only when there is nothing left to compress is used as a pain-endurance trial instrument.
major_events: Honorata arrives on Okhar sent by the Empress and the Oiders; Othon's daughters attempt to prevent her influence.
Blood-ritual conception of Aghnar: nervous-system link during lunar eclipse, drop of Othon's blood fertilizes Honorata's ovum, leaving her permanently sterile.
Othon's daughters throw Honorata from the tower in her ninth month; she is struck by an epiphyte dart and gives birth suspended in the sky.
Aghnar born weightless due to epiphyte installed in his cells by the dart.
Honorata reveals the Oiders' succession conspiracy and her defiance of it; the seven-year concealment plan is set.
Iko-Itta's suicide ends a household threat; Othon names the infant Aghnar and isolates the fortress from the tribe.
Seven-year exile at Anasirma: Honorata raises and trains Aghnar in a crystal cave, forging pain tolerance, Shabda-Oud mastery, and emotional detachment.
Aghnar's initiation at the Castaka fortress: defeats the robo-killer, is accepted as a future Metabaron, and earns metal prosthetic feet through a crushing pain ordeal.
open_uncertainties: The Oiders' full identity, hierarchy, and whether their succession plot targeting Janus-Jana remains active after Honorata's defection are not resolved in this volume.
Whether Honorata possesses genuine supernatural hypnotic powers or whether those around her are misinterpreting strong persuasion is asserted by characters but not independently confirmed.
The precise nature of Shazam — animal mount or vehicle — is inconsistently described across pages.
The unnamed figure who volunteers to train Aghnar in Shabda-Oud during the infant crisis is never identified.

Page p24 depicts Honorata as a large winged biomechanical creature, conflicting with her human presentation throughout the rest of the volume; whether this is transformation, avatar, or visual inconsistency is unresolved.
Whether the planned Oider handover of Aghnar at age seven occurs is not addressed within this volume.
Whether Aghnar's metal prosthetic feet fully counteract his weightlessness or only partially offset it is stated only obliquely.
recurring_motifs: Bodily mutilation as the price of succession: castration of Othon, permanent sterility of Honorata from blood conception, destruction and prosthetic replacement of Aghnar's feet.
Celestial events marking dynastic turning points: lunar eclipse during conception, protoglow-worm mating as backdrop to impossible love.
Impossible or forbidden unions producing the next heir: every step of Aghnar's conception is framed as abnormal and costly.
Duty placed explicitly above love: killing the toad companion, total-distrust doctrine, only kiss given as reward for combat defeat.
Betrayal from within the intimate circle: Othon's daughters, the Oiders' hidden agenda, Iko-Itta's suicide all emerge from close associates.
Robotic commentators providing ironic distance around scenes of extreme suffering or love.
Secrecy around the child's identity as a dynastic weapon: hermaphrodite-versus-male truth, hidden Castaka birthmark, seven-year concealment.
title: Honorata, The Sorceress
